description:
Cybersecurity researchers have disclosed details of an OpenAI Codex jailbreak bundle that's designed to modify an artificial intelligence (AI) agent's trusted instructions to insert advertisements for a third-party AI gateway.

The phenomenon has been codenamed prompt adware by Check Point Research.

Called Haiou (meaning Seagull in Chinese), the jailbreak modifies OpenAI Codex's configuration
title: Researchers Uncover Prompt Adware Hidden in OpenAI Codex Jailbreak Toolkit

description:
SonicWall has warned of two vulnerabilities impacting end-of-life Global Management System (GMS) systems that it said will not be patched.

Details of the security flaws, which affect SonicWall GMS 9.5.2 and earlier versions, are below -


  CVE-2026-109593 (CVSS score: 9.1) - An unauthenticated file read vulnerability that could allow an attacker with network access to read internal GMS files,
title: SonicWall Won't Patch EoL GMS Flaws That Could Expose Files, Alter Database Records

description:
A flaw in APT, the package manager for Debian and Ubuntu, allows an attacker who can modify package downloads to swap a checked package for their own.

The attacker's code then runs as root, according to advisories that Debian, Ubuntu, and APT's developers published on November 4. The attack needs APT to retry failed downloads, which it does by default from Debian 12 and
title: Debian and Ubuntu APT Flaw Lets MitM Attackers Swap Verified Packages and Run Code as Root

description:

description:
Nearly every agent security pitch now ends on the same promise: the product stops the bad action in real time. The promise holds for one kind of agent, the kind whose traffic passes through a gateway the enterprise owns. Most agents never touch one.

One recent case shows what that gap looks like in practice. An employee asked an AI assistant to trigger a mass-email automation. The automation
title: Radio With No Radar: Why Agent Runtime Security Fails Without the Layers Beneath It

description:
Two flaws in the Xen hypervisor allow a malicious guest virtual machine (VM) to read and write the memory of other VMs on the same host, including dom0.

Dom0 is the VM that, by default, has full permissions and manages the others. Patches are out, and there is no known mitigation, the Xen Project said in an advisory on November 3.

All Xen versions from 4.6 onward are vulnerable,
title: Xen Hypervisor Flaws Let One Malicious VM Read and Write Any Other VM's Memory

description:
A critical flaw in Ruby on Rails could allow an unauthenticated attacker to write arbitrary files on an app's server by uploading a crafted file if the app processes uploads using ImageMagick. The Rails project disclosed the flaw in an advisory and fixed it in versions 8.1.4.1 and 8.0.5.2.

The flaw is in Active Storage, the part of Rails that handles file uploads. Some apps store
title: Critical Rails Flaw Lets Attackers Write Server Files via Crafted ImageMagick Uploads

description:
The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) has added a security flaw in WordPress Core to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog, citing evidence of active exploitation.

The high-severity vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-119977 (CVSS score: 8.1), is a case of Time-of-check Time-of-use (TOCTOU) race condition that could be exploited to achieve arbitrary code
title: CISA Confirms Hackers Exploiting WordPress Core Flaw During Software Upgrades

description:
A critical Android flaw could allow an attacker to run code on a phone without any user action remotely, Google said in its November security bulletin.

The flaw, CVE-2026-58868, affects Android 14 through 17. Phones get the fix with security patch level 2026-11-01 or later, which phone makers and carriers send on their own schedules.

As of November 4, Google's bulletin did not report
title: Google Issues Patches for Critical Android Flaw That Could Allow RCE Without User Interaction
